decisions.rationale: The declared 500-873 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It states John McVie's melodic bass was replaced while he was on vacation by Lindsey's simple quarter-note bassline and says this was the start of Lindsey calling the shots; the artifact finalUrl is the exact Wayback replay form with embedded https://.

The declared 1281-1906 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It identifies Sly Stone's Pit as the spare piano room where Stevie worked and came out with Dreams, then states an eight-bar loop of Mick's playing created a hypnotic effect.

The declared 2260-2920 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It says the song was called Brushes because of a planned brushed snare part and describes restringing Lindsey's guitar every 20 minutes for the best sound on each picking part.

The declared 3571-4048 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It says Don't Stop was Christine's song, improved dramatically after her duet suggestion to Lindsey, and that the band kept changing the end background vocals.

The declared 4143-4919 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It describes Lindsey beating his acoustic guitar and screaming, then says both guitar solos were comped from seven or eight tracks and sounded seamless rather than fully composed.

The declared 5680-6383 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It states the concert-recital recording idea, the use of Zellerbach Auditorium, Christine on a nine-foot Steinway, and 15 piano tracks with two close mics and the rest distant.

The declared 6536-7491 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It says The Chain was the first song worked on, began as Christine's Keep Me There, and that three weeks before wrapping Lindsey connected it by taking verses apart, playing Dobro, and asking Mick for straight quarter-note kick.

The declared 7999-8629 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It says the part was originally on Christine's Yamaha electric piano, then used Clavinet through wah-wah, with Mick working the pedal while Christine played.

The declared 9124-9605 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It says Silver Springs could not make the record because it was too long, a shorter uptempo song was needed, and the track was cut without Stevie before she added vocals later.

The declared 9827-10378 offset exactly matches the retained extract. It identifies Oh Daddy as an early track likely done after The Chain, Christine on organ, Lindsey's guitar lines with a possible Strat, and the Rick Turner-built Stratoblaster boost used for a nastier edge.

The declared 11273-11692 offset exactly matches the retained extract and is bound to Gold Dust Woman fact-1. It describes typical Stevie songs as 10 or 12 minutes with endless verses, then says the job became editing sections and cutting material that meant something personal to her.

The declared 11693-12497 offset exactly matches the retained extract and is separately bound to Gold Dust Woman fact-2. It states Stevie did coyote-like howling at the end and that Mick broke sheets of glass in a miked room to accentuate her vocals.
